en.title: Depth-Weighted Sum of a Nested List
en.description:
The elements of a nested list are integers or lists. Integers in the outermost list have depth 1, and each additional level of list nesting adds 1 to the depth. Output the sum of every integer multiplied by its depth; negative numbers and empty sublists are allowed.

The standard input, this site's constraints, the examples, and the test data were independently compiled by CSWork.
en.input: One line with a valid JSON nested list whose outermost level has 1..50 elements; each integer is in −100..100, and no integer is deeper than 50. This site limits the total number of list and integer nodes to at most 100000, and the input to at most 2000000 characters.
en.explanation:
Example 1: the four 1s have depth 2 and the integer 2 has depth 1, so the sum is 4×1×2+2×1=10.

Example 2: 1, 4, and 6 have depths 1, 2, and 3 respectively, so the sum is 1+8+18=27.

Example 3: the only integer, 0, contributes 0×1=0.
hints: After parsing the list, use an explicit stack holding lists and their depths; an integer contributes its value times the depth, and a sublist is pushed with the depth plus one.
